title: The World's Biggest Electric Plane Just Took Off!
summary: Imagine a plane that runs on batteries, just like your tablet or toy car. The world's largest electric plane just made its first flight! It's called the X1, and it's made by a company called Heart Aerospace. The X1 has a wingspan of 106 feet—that's longer than a basketball court! It weighs more than 25,000 pounds, about the same as an empty school bus. The plane took off from an airport in upstate New York and flew for 27 minutes, reaching 1,100 feet high. It had only a pilot on board, no passengers. The company says the flight used just $5 worth of electricity. That sounds amazing, but it doesn't include other costs like paying the pilot or fixing the plane. Heart Aerospace wants to build a bigger plane called the ES-30 that can carry 30 passengers. They hope to start flying it by 2031. Electric planes are cleaner than regular planes, which pollute the air. But batteries are heavy, so electric planes can't fly very far yet. The X1 can only go about 125 miles on battery power. That's why Heart is planning a hybrid plane that also has a gas engine to go farther—up to 500 miles. That could be perfect for short trips between nearby cities. So while we won't be flying electric across the ocean anytime soon, this test flight is a big step toward cleaner air travel!
why_it_matters: Cleaner electric planes could help protect the air you breathe, so this test flight is a sign that your future travel might pollute less.

background_read: Heart Aerospace is a Swedish company that is trying to build electric planes for short flights.
Regular jet planes burn fuel that pollutes the air, so engineers are looking for cleaner ways to fly.
Small electric planes have flown before, but building one as big as an empty school bus is a much harder challenge.
The X1's first flight took place in upstate New York, a region north of New York City.
Article_Structure: WHO: Heart Aerospace, the company that built the X1 electric plane
WHAT: The X1, the world's largest electric plane, made its first flight using only battery power
WHERE: An airport in upstate New York
WHY: To take a step toward cleaner short-distance air travel and build a 30-passenger plane by 2031

perspectives.description: Heart Aerospace and clean-energy fans are excited because electric planes could reduce pollution from short flights.
Some travelers might be disappointed because the X1 cannot fly very far yet and carried no passengers, so electric flying is still limited.
Engineers see this first flight as a small but important step, because solving battery weight will decide whether electric planes can grow.
